live_web_research.page_text: [2609.30557] Auditing Latent-Space Monitors for Autonomous Driving Skip to main content Search arXiv Press Enter to search · Advanced search --> Computer Science > Robotics arXiv:2609.30557 (cs) [Submitted on 24 Sep 2026] Title: Auditing Latent-Space Monitors for Autonomous Driving Authors: Nikhil Kamalkumar Advani , Vishwajeet Shivaji Hogale , Saurav Kumar View a PDF of the paper titled Auditing Latent-Space Monitors for Autonomous Driving, by Nikhil Kamalkumar Advani and 2 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Runtime failure monitors can use a model's internal representations to anticipate failures. We audit this monitoring strategy across two autonomous-driving tasks: online vectorized map generation with LaneSegNet and end-to-end planning with VAD. We find that frame-level errors are predictable at inference in both tasks. For LaneSegNet, a supervised latent probe reaches Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve (AUROC) 0.780 for high Chamfer error; to our knowledge, this is the first post-hoc frame-level failure monitor for online vectorized map generation. For VAD, a supervised planning-latent probe reaches AUROC 0.868 for mean-ADE failure. Our audit shows that internal access is not necessary for strong failure prediction. A monitor using only LaneSegNet's prediction outputs reaches AUROC 0.825, while for VAD, ego state, driving command, and the planner's predicted trajectory reach 0.924 on the same mean-ADE endpoint. Adding latent features to either baseline yields no statistically resolved improvement. This observation persists across a broad suite of planning failure endpoints, including endpoints whose labels depend on geometry unavailable to the non-latent baseline. Thus, predicting failure from an internal representation does not establish that the representation provides useful information beyond observable inputs and outputs. We propose an evaluation protocol for testing the incremental value of latent access and release our per-frame failure endpoint labels. article.body:
Research audit tests latent-space failure monitors, not a vehicle deployment

Nikhil Kamalkumar Advani, Vishwajeet Shivaji Hogale and Saurav Kumar’s paper, submitted to arXiv on 24 September 2026, is a research audit rather than a pilot, limited service or commercial operation; no operator or geography is specified. It evaluates runtime monitors on online vectorized map generation with LaneSegNet and end-to-end planning with VAD, rather than a vehicle’s road-domain sensor stack or geofence. The reported evidence is model-level: latent probes reached AUROC 0.780 for LaneSegNet high Chamfer error and 0.868 for VAD mean-ADE failure, while output-only baselines reached 0.825 and 0.924 respectively; no road miles, incidents or safety-driver data are reported. The authors propose an evaluation protocol and release per-frame failure labels, with no regulatory approval or commercial next step established.
